applied.problem: Two of the three free cases (overdamped, critical) do not swing, so 'free swings come in three kinds' clashes with i6; and 'they add to zero at every moment' fails once a push or supply drives it (i7), where the sum equals the push.

Setting the three terms equal to zero, and inertia = minus store at a still start, hold only with no push or supply; after i7 a driven spring or circuit has the push on the other side, and Dan keeps this method to use.
With a heavy brake the flywheel creeps back without swinging (i6), and the loop may not swing either, so 'add a brake, and it swings back and forth as the loop does' is too absolute.
